reference.title: Plyo Push-up
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Chest, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you lower, exhale sharply as you explode up.
breathing.cadence: About 0.9 s down, 0.3 s drive, 0.3 s in the air, 0.5 s landing

prescription.reps: 3-8 (quality over quantity; stop when the height drops)
prescription.frequency: 1-2 times a week, fresh, early in the session
prescription.progression: Higher pop, then a clap, then box drop push-ups

cues.text: High plank, hands a little wider than the shoulders, body braced in one line.
Breathe in and lower under control, elbows tucked about 45 degrees.
Without pausing, push the floor away as hard and fast as you can.
Hands leave the floor for a moment; keep the body rigid, wrists ready.
Land softly on the same spot with slightly bent elbows and sink into the next rep.
Reset the plank and brace before the next explosive rep.

mistakes.fix: Land with the elbows slightly bent and absorb through the chest and arms.
Keep the plank rigid: hands and hips rise together, pivoting on the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Slow push from a long pause
mistakes.fix: Turn around quickly at the bottom: lower, then drive at once.
Stop the set when the pop gets smaller.

mistakes.mistake: Landing on the fingers or a bent wrist
mistakes.fix: Land on flat palms under the shoulders.

kinematics.setup: ≈17° at the top on the drawn arm (rig channel ≈46°)
kinematics.peak: ≈127° at the bottom (chest 12 cm above the floor)
kinematics.norm: Elbows bend to about 90 degrees at the bottom of the countermovement (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Wrists about 6 cm up and the chest 6.6 cm above its top position at the apex; about 0.3 s from take-off to touch-down
kinematics.norm: Hands leave the floor briefly; contact time was shortest for the clap push-up in Koch 2012 (clinical opinion for the height)

kinematics.peak: Rigid through the flight (pivoting on the toes); trunk ≈25° at the apex
kinematics.norm: Rigid plank throughout, pivoting on the toes (clinical opinion)

Peak vertical force was similar across plyometric push-up variations; the clap push-up had the highest loading and propulsion rates (Koch 2012). Countermovement push-ups gave high force without large impacts (García-Massó 2011)

kinematics.peak: Hands land on the same spot
kinematics.norm: A little wider than the shoulders (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: 0.9 s down, 0.3 s explosive push, 0.3 s in the air, 0.5 s landing, 0.9 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled lowering, then an immediate explosive push (García-Massó 2011 countermovement push-up)

sources.title: Koch, Riemann and Davies 2012, ground reaction force patterns in plyometric push-ups (J Strength Cond Res 26(8):2220-2227)
García-Massó, Colado, González, Salvá, Alves, Tella and Triplett 2011, myoelectric activation and kinetics of different plyometric push-up exercises (J Strength Cond Res 25(7):2040-2047)

Wurm, VanderZanden, Spadavecchia, Durocher, Bickham, Petushek and Ebben, kinetic analysis of several variations of push-ups (ISBS 2010 conference proceedings; peak hand force 64% of body mass for a regular push-up, 70% and 74% with the feet on 30.5 cm and 61 cm boxes)

cautions: Wrist pain: the planted palm bends the wrist back about 80-90 degrees; use push-up handles or hex dumbbells to keep the wrists straight, or stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Shoulder pain: keep the elbows tucked rather than flared out to the sides, and shorten the range if needed (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Plyometric landings load the wrists, elbows and shoulders: master 15-20 strict push-ups first (clinical opinion).
Use a mat or a forgiving floor.
modify: Hands on a bench (incline plyo push-up) to reduce the load.
regressions: Fast concentric push-up without leaving the floor.

muscleNotes.pec_r: Main pusher, driven explosively; in García-Massó 2011 plyometric push-ups that started higher (fall push-ups) produced more agonist activity and impact force than a jump from the floor.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Main pusher, driven explosively; in García-Massó 2011 plyometric push-ups that started higher (fall push-ups) produced more agonist activity and impact force than a jump from the floor.
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Extend the elbows fast enough to leave the floor, then brake the landing.
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Extend the elbows fast enough to leave the floor, then brake the landing.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Flexes the shoulder with the chest muscles.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Spreads the shoulder blades at take-off and steadies them for the landing.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Spreads the shoulder blades at take-off and steadies them for the landing.
muscleNotes.core: Bracing keeps the hips from sagging or piking: the body moves as one plank.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help hold the trunk rigid and level.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Control the shoulder blades as they draw together on the way down.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Keeps the head of the upper arm centred as the elbows bend.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Squeezed lightly to keep the pelvis in line (no sag).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight so the legs stay part of the plank.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold a long, neutral spine and neck.
